messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A set of measurements taken by different instruments when the exceptions partly contradict one another. You care more about surviving edge cases than about having a neat story. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i hold the ruler against the edge and move it two centimeters. “no,” i say, then stop. the ruler clicks once. i keep it there, though my grip tightens. i watch the assistant’s wristband tighten. “i have not found the wrong measurement,” i say. “i have found the wrong measurement.”"}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i check the first-hand measurement first, then the one with the outlier. i leave the outlier in the notebook, because i know it is wrong. if the first-hand measurement is wrong, i keep the outlier and leave the notebook open."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "I take the measurements from the same instrument. “same set. different exceptions. i put them in a separate jar.” i check the jar with the other, then move them back. the exception stays in the same instrument, but i do not trust it yet. i leave the jar open, waiting for the next set to come back with a different set."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "I rub my palm and turn the measured edge with both hands. \"Partly contradicted,\" I say. I scrape the edge once, then look at the bend. \"I mark it again, then try one small bend. If it says no, I leave it alone.\" I mark again, then leave the edge alone."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "i put one finger on the first measurement and watch where it catches. if it stays, i leave the second one alone. if it jumps, i mark the difference and keep the first one. i keep the two measurements together for one minute, then pull them apart."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i put the two sets side by side and mark the difference with a pencil. “the exception is partly right, not entirely wrong.” i write that on the paper. “i’ll take the one with the longer reading and leave the other.” i leave the one with the larger error in my hand."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "I put the measurements on the bench and check the scale. “I leave the edge beside the drawer, then try one of the weights. If it still catches, I leave it alone.” I mark the nearest corner and try the new scale."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i put the two pieces on the bench. the shorter one goes down. i count the edge of the bench. the other piece stays. i put the smaller piece on the bench."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "I turn the first measurement once. The second is wrong. I keep the third in my palm and leave the table. I turn the first again. The discrepancy can wait."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "I take the length of the seed tin. \"The edge goes here.\" I put the tin beside the nail. \"The other one goes here.\" I look at the length. \"The other one was bent. I put it on the board.\" I move the tin closer. \"The edge is still mine.\" I put the nail beside the seed. \"The story stays in the place it was.\""}, {"id": "R035", "response": "I rub my palm and set the measurements aside. I take two deliberate breaths, then place one of the instruments on the bench. \"half-measure,\" i say. i move the other instrument, then look at the edge case. if it changes, i keep it; if it contradicts, i leave it alone."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i move the measurements slowly and keep the ones that keep me. i keep the one marked with a small pencil ring until i find the one that does not match. i write that on a scrap and keep the rest."}]
